review_locator: PMCID:PMC8105286, Biophysics of Notch Signaling, ligand-receptor binding/structural basis section
primary_title: Intrinsic selectivity of Notch 1 for Delta-like 4 over Delta-like 1
decision_basis: The review identifies DLL1 as a Notch1 ligand, and the cited primary study directly measures calcium-dependent DLL1-NOTCH1 binding and DLL1-dependent Notch1 reporter activation using recombinant and cell-based systems.
limitations_preserved: Preserve membrane-presentation, calcium, ligand-density, and DLL1-versus-DLL4 selectivity boundaries; no SCI receiver or reverse DLL1 intracellular claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2745238, Structure-based view of epidermal growth factor receptor regulation; PMCID:PMC4452390, A Structural Perspective on the Regulation of the EGF Receptor
primary_title: Crystal structure of the complex of human epidermal growth factor and receptor extracellular domains
decision_basis: The reviews identify the ligand-induced EGFR dimer model, and the cited primary structure directly resolves a 2:2 human EGF-EGFR ectodomain complex with receptor-mediated dimerization verified by mutagenesis.
limitations_preserved: Direct extracellular assembly/activation topology only; preserve 2:2 ligand-receptor stoichiometry and do not infer a universal downstream adaptor or SCI context.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5958381, Internal Affairs: Tenascin-C as a Clinically Relevant, Endogenous Driver of Innate Immunity; PMCID:PMC2778592, The role of tenascin-C in tissue injury and tumorigenesis
primary_title: Mapping tenascin-C interaction with toll-like receptor 4 reveals a new subset of endogenous inflammatory triggers
decision_basis: The reviews identify tenascin-C as an endogenous TLR4 activator, and the cited primary study maps three FBG-domain sites that directly and cooperatively interact with TLR4 and induce NF-kB/cytokine responses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the FBG-domain/fragment and TLR4-complex context, endotoxin controls, and sterile-inflammation model limits; no SCI receiver weighting or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2826542, An Overview of IL-7 Biology and Its Use in Immunotherapy, IL-7 and Jak/Stat section; PMCID:PMC2040031, Interlinking Interleukin-7
primary_title: Interleukin-7 can induce the activation of Jak 1, Jak 3 and STAT 5 proteins in murine T cells
decision_basis: The reviews place JAK1 on IL-7Ralpha and JAK3 on the common gamma chain, and the cited primary study shows rapid, dose-dependent IL-7-induced JAK1 and JAK3 tyrosine phosphorylation in murine T cells.
limitations_preserved: Receptor-associated kinase activation only; preserve IL-7Ralpha/common-gamma subunit assignment and T-cell comparator scope, with no SCI or direct cytokine-to-kinase binding claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2826542, An Overview of IL-7 Biology and Its Use in Immunotherapy, IL-7 and Jak/Stat section; PMCID:PMC2040031, Interlinking Interleukin-7
primary_title: Interleukin-7 can induce the activation of Jak 1, Jak 3 and STAT 5 proteins in murine T cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify STAT5 as a principal IL-7 receptor output, and the cited primary study shows IL-7-induced STAT5 phosphorylation/DNA-binding activity correlated with growth-promoting effects in murine T cells.
limitations_preserved: Bound to STAT5 relay/program in IL-7 receptor systems; do not infer terminal-TF status, universal STAT exclusivity, or SCI glial function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4489423, The molecular basis of IL-10 function, receptor assembly section; PMCID:PMC2997900, The IL-10 family of cytokines and their receptors
primary_title: Structure-based decoupling of the pro- and anti-inflammatory functions of interleukin-10
decision_basis: The reviews describe sequential IL-10R1/IL-10R2 signaling-complex assembly, and the cited primary cryo-EM study resolves the IL-10-IL-10Ralpha-IL-10Rbeta complex and its composite receptor interface.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the 2:2:2 receptor-complex architecture and engineered/stabilized structural context; do not infer native-cell stoichiometry or SCI receiver weighting.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4489423, The molecular basis of IL-10 function, from receptor structure to the onset of signaling; PMCID:PMC2997900, The IL-10 family of cytokines and their receptors
primary_title: Stat3 recruitment by two distinct ligand-induced, tyrosine-phosphorylated docking sites in the interleukin-10 receptor intracellular domain; An essential role for Stat3 in the inhibition of TNF production by interleukin-10
decision_basis: The reviews identify STAT3 as an IL-10 receptor output, and the cited primary studies show receptor-tail Tyr427/Tyr477 docking requirements for STAT3 plus JAK1/STAT3-dependent IL-10 responses in macrophages.
limitations_preserved: Receptor-tail/STAT3 pathway layer only; preserve IL10RA/IL10RB receptor-complex context and do not infer direct ligand-to-STAT3 binding or SCI glial specificity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6596353, IL-1 family structural-signaling review; PMCID:PMC12337794, IL-18 receptor review
primary_title: Structural basis for the specific recognition of IL-18 by its alpha receptor
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-18R1 as the primary ligand-binding subunit, and the cited primary crystal structure directly resolves mature human IL-18 bound to the IL-18R1 ectodomain and maps the recognition interface.
limitations_preserved: Direct primary-receptor binding only; preserve mature IL-18 processing and separate IL18RAP accessory-receptor assembly, with no SCI receiver or terminal-TF inference.
